_comment: CDC scenario INITIAL LOAD UNDER LIVE CHANGES, --trx-mode nested: MySQL CDC over the binlog (ROW format, FULL row images, gtid_mode=ON), each publisher a replica with a server_id of its own; a change to a keyless table names its row by every column. The binlog has no row for what an ON DELETE CASCADE takes and no event for an UPDATE that changes nothing: --cascades unlogged --noops unlogged. An initial load pins its GTID position under a brief global read lock, so no change is both loaded and replayed. The initial load is taken while modify-data churns, its transactions nests 8 deep, each begun inside the one before it and committed inside it too -- commits in reverse start order. STAGES: (1) domains -- create the mysqlcdc domain, install employeescdc, load the m seed (10k rows a table), its operations appended to ${xp:dir}/ops.jsonl; (2) actions, tagged live -- `sentinel-data --key after-create-data`, then `churn` in the background: 20 passes a second apart of `modify-data --ops Mix --sets 250 --trx-mode nested --trx-concurrency 8`, every set one transaction of one verb over its tables -- inserts, updates (accounts' moving its key), deletes; it keeps running through the stages below; (3) collections and (4) functions -- register mysqlcdc_initial_load_live (initial_load=True), which STARTS it: its load is taken over tables changing under it; (5) actions, tagged live -- wait for churn, then `sentinel-data --key after-churn`; (6) sentinel -- hold until both keys arrive; (7) actions, tagged check -- scripts/verify_cdc_ops.py --check state: the load plus every change applied in commit order as the connector deduplicates must leave each table as the whole trail does; no change the load holds arrives again, on any table; nothing of audit; (8) monitor. Generated by gen_suites.py. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite cdc/mysqlcdc_initial_load_live_nested --keep`.
